definition: The HPA axis is the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, a biological system linking the hypothalamus, pituitary, and adrenal glands. In this packet, its functioning is described as something that can become dysregulated in some cases of cancer-related fatigue.

provenance.scope: Source record C165676; pinned source text

reasons: The packet text provided does not define the HPA axis as specifically linking the hypothalamus, pituitary, and adrenal glands; that substantive structural description is not supported by the packet.

The packet only states that HPA axis functioning may be dysregulated in certain cases of cancer-related fatigue; the definition’s opening statement about what the HPA axis is in general is not supported by the packet.

Because the packet context is about bupropion and includes only a brief mention of “normalize hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis functioning,” the definition’s broader, general description is unsupported.

The packet supports the full form “hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis,” but it does not explicitly support the added explanation that it is “a biological system linking the hypothalamus, pituitary, and adrenal glands.”
The packet context is about bupropion and cancer-related fatigue; the definition should avoid presenting the HPA axis as a standalone clinical description beyond what the source text supports.
